page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-56 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides 56 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 28 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It features 224.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core. This configuration does not bundle local NVMe SSD storage or hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core processing and memory performance. The instance achieves top-25% results in stress-ng multi-core CPU testing and Geekbench multi-core execution, alongside a top-10% Passmark memory score. Cryptographic capabilities are supported by hardware-accelerated AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instructions, leading to strong performance in Passmark CPU encryption tests. For data-intensive workloads, the system demonstrates strong throughput in Redis SET operations, processing 61.92 million operations per second, and strong database operations in Passmark. Single-core performance, static web serving throughput, and large-block memory bandwidth remain in the average tier.

Given its high core density and dedicated CPU allocation, the c2d-standard-56 is highly cost-efficient for parallelized, compute-intensive workloads that do not require local storage or GPU acceleration. It is well-suited for software compilation, ray tracing, image processing, and database operations. Additionally, the instance supports moderate LLM inference tasks, showing strong text generation speeds for small and medium models, though prompt processing speeds scale average.
